sourceDate.text: 高祖十年七月，太上皇崩
高祖十年七月，太上皇崩

units.zh: 韓王信者，故韓襄王孽孫也，長八尺五寸。
units.en: Han Xin, the King of Han, was a descendant of the former King Xiang of Han through a concubine's line. He stood eight feet five inches tall.
units.literal: Han King Xin was a descendant through a concubine's line of the former King Xiang of Han, and was eight chi five cun tall.

units.zh: 及項梁之立楚後懷王也，燕、齊、趙、魏皆已前王，唯韓無有後，故立韓諸公子橫陽君成為韓王，欲以撫定韓故地。
units.en: When Xiang Liang installed the later King Huai of Chu, the states of Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had all already restored their former royal lines. Only Han had no surviving heir, so they established Cheng, the Lord of Hengyang and a prince of the Han royal house, as King of Han, intending to pacify and settle the former Han territories.
units.literal: When Xiang Liang established the later King Huai of Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had all already restored their former kings; only Han had no heir, so they established the Lord of Hengyang, Cheng, one of the princes of Han, as King of Han, wishing to pacify and settle the former territory of Han.

units.zh: 項梁敗死定陶，成奔懷王。
units.en: When Xiang Liang was defeated and killed at Dingtao, Cheng fled to King Huai.
units.literal: Xiang Liang was defeated and died at Dingtao; Cheng fled to King Huai.

units.zh: 沛公引兵擊陽城，使張良以韓司徒降下韓故地，得信，以為韓將，將其兵從沛公入武關。
units.en: The Lord of Pei led his forces to attack Yangcheng and dispatched Zhang Liang, serving as the Minister of Education of Han, to secure the surrender of the former Han territories. There he obtained Han Xin's services, appointed him as a general of Han, and had him lead his troops to follow the Lord of Pei through the Wu Pass.
units.literal: The Lord of Pei led troops to attack Yangcheng, sent Zhang Liang as the Han Minister of Education to receive the surrender of Han's former territory, obtained Xin, made him a Han general, and had him lead troops following the Lord of Pei through Wu Pass.

units.zh: 沛公立為漢王，韓信從入漢中，乃說漢王曰：「項王王諸將近地，而王獨遠居此，此左遷也。
units.en: When the Lord of Pei was established as King of Han, Han Xin followed him into Hanzhong. He counseled the King of Han, saying: 'The King of Xiang has enfeoffed all his other generals with territories close at hand, yet Your Majesty alone has been banished to this remote place. This is a demotion.
units.literal: When the Lord of Pei was established as King of Han, Han Xin followed into Hanzhong and counseled the King of Han saying: 'The King of Xiang enfeoffed all his generals with nearby territories, yet Your Majesty alone dwells far away here; this is a demotion.

units.zh: 士卒皆山東人，跂而望歸，及其鋒東鄉，可以爭天下。」
units.en: Your soldiers are all men from east of the mountains who stand on tiptoe gazing homeward. If you harness their eagerness and march east, you can contend for the empire.'
units.literal: The soldiers are all men from east of the mountains; they stand on tiptoe gazing homeward. If you take advantage of their sharp eagerness and turn east, you can contend for the realm.'

units.zh: 漢王還定三秦，乃許信為韓王，先拜信為韓太尉，將兵略韓地。
units.en: When the King of Han returned to conquer the Three Qin kingdoms, he promised to make Han Xin the King of Han. First, he appointed Xin as Grand Commandant of Han and sent him to lead troops to take the Han territories.
units.literal: When the King of Han returned and pacified the Three Qin, he then promised Xin the title of King of Han, first appointing Xin as Grand Commandant of Han, and had him lead troops to take the Han territory.

units.zh: 項籍之封諸王皆就國，韓王成以不從無功，不遣就國，更以為列侯。
units.en: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed all the kings and they went to their domains, King Cheng of Han had not accompanied Xiang Ji and had no merit to his name, so he was not allowed to proceed to his domain. Instead, he was demoted to the rank of marquis.
units.literal: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed all the kings and they each went to their kingdoms, King Cheng of Han, because he had not followed and had no merit, was not sent to his kingdom and was instead made a marquis.

units.zh: 及聞漢遣韓信略韓地，乃令故項籍游吳時吳令鄭昌為韓王以距漢。
units.en: When Xiang Ji heard that Han had dispatched Han Xin to take the Han territories, he appointed Zheng Chang, who had served as the Magistrate of Wu when Xiang Ji was traveling in Wu, as King of Han to resist the Han forces.
units.literal: When he heard that Han had sent Han Xin to take the Han territory, he appointed Zheng Chang, who had been the Magistrate of Wu when Xiang Ji traveled in Wu, as King of Han to resist Han.

units.zh: 漢二年，韓信略定韓十餘城。
units.en: In the second year of the Han dynasty, Han Xin conquered more than ten cities in the Han territory.
units.literal: In the second year of Han, Han Xin conquered and pacified more than ten cities of Han.

units.zh: 漢王至河南，韓信急擊韓王昌陽城。
units.en: When the King of Han arrived at Henan, Han Xin launched a swift attack on King Chang of Han at Yangcheng.
units.literal: When the King of Han reached Henan, Han Xin urgently attacked King Chang of Han at Yangcheng.

units.zh: 昌降，漢王乃立韓信為韓王，常將韓兵從。
units.en: Chang surrendered, and the King of Han thereupon established Han Xin as King of Han. Xin regularly led the Han troops in the king's service.
units.literal: Chang surrendered, and the King of Han then established Han Xin as King of Han; he constantly led Han troops in service.

units.zh: 三年，漢王出滎陽，韓王信、周苛等守滎陽。
units.en: In the third year, when the King of Han left Xingyang, Han Xin the King of Han, along with Zhou Ke and others, was left to defend Xingyang.
units.literal: In the third year, the King of Han left Xingyang; Han King Xin, Zhou Ke, and others defended Xingyang.

units.zh: 及楚敗滎陽，信降楚，已而得亡，復歸漢，漢復立以為韓王，竟從擊破項籍，天下定。
units.en: When Chu defeated Xingyang, Xin surrendered to Chu. Later he managed to escape and returned to Han, and the Han court restored him as King of Han. He ultimately joined in the campaign that defeated Xiang Ji, and the realm was settled.
units.literal: When Chu defeated Xingyang, Xin surrendered to Chu; afterward he managed to escape, returned to Han, and Han again established him as King of Han. He ultimately followed in defeating Xiang Ji, and the realm was settled.

units.zh: 五年春，遂與剖符為韓王，王潁川。
units.en: In the spring of the fifth year, he was formally invested as King of Han with the splitting of the tally, and he ruled over Yingchuan.
units.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, he was thereupon invested as King of Han with the splitting of the tally, and ruled over Yingchuan.

units.zh: 明年春，上以韓信材武，所王北近鞏、洛，南迫宛、葉，東有淮陽，皆天下勁兵處，乃詔徙韓王信王太原以北，備御胡，都晉陽。
units.en: The following spring, the Emperor, noting that Han Xin was a man of martial talent and that his kingdom lay close to Gong and Luoyang in the north, bordered Wan and Ye in the south, and included Huaiyang in the east—all strategic positions for the empire's most formidable troops—issued a decree transferring the King of Han to rule north of Taiyuan, charged with defending against the Hu nomads, with his capital at Jinyang.
units.literal: The next spring, the Emperor, considering that Han Xin was talented and martial, and that his kingdom was close to Gong and Luo in the north, bordered Wan and Ye in the south, and held Huaiyang in the east—all locations of the realm's crack troops—issued a decree to transfer the King of Han to rule north of Taiyuan, to defend against the Hu, with his capital at Jinyang.

units.zh: 信上書曰：「國被邊，匈奴數入，晉陽去塞遠，請治馬邑。」
units.en: Xin submitted a memorial saying: 'My kingdom lies along the frontier, and the Xiongnu invade frequently. Jinyang is too far from the border passes. I request permission to govern from Mayi.'
units.literal: Xin submitted a memorial saying: 'The kingdom borders the frontier; the Xiongnu frequently invade; Jinyang is far from the border passes. I request to administer from Mayi.'

units.zh: 上許之，信乃徙治馬邑。
units.en: The Emperor granted his request, and Xin moved his seat of government to Mayi.
units.literal: The Emperor permitted it, and Xin thereupon moved to administer from Mayi.

units.zh: 秋，匈奴冒頓大圍信，信數使使胡求和解。
units.en: That autumn, the Xiongnu Chanyu Modu besieged Xin with a massive force. Xin sent envoy after envoy to the Xiongnu to negotiate peace.
units.literal: In autumn, the Xiongnu Chanyu Modu laid a great siege around Xin; Xin repeatedly sent envoys to the Hu to seek a peace settlement.

units.zh: 漢發兵救之，疑信數閒使，有二心，使人責讓信。
units.en: Han dispatched troops to relieve him, but suspected that Xin's frequent secret embassies meant he harbored divided loyalties, and sent a messenger to rebuke him.
units.literal: Han dispatched troops to rescue him, but suspected Xin of frequently sending secret envoys and harboring divided loyalties, and sent someone to rebuke and reproach Xin.

units.zh: 信恐誅，因與匈奴約共攻漢，反，以馬邑降胡，擊太原。
units.en: Xin, fearing execution, made a pact with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Han. He rebelled, surrendered Mayi to the Xiongnu, and struck at Taiyuan.
units.literal: Xin, fearing execution, thereupon made a pact with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Han, rebelled, surrendered Mayi to the Hu, and attacked Taiyuan.

units.zh: 七年冬，上自往擊，破信軍銅鞮，斬其將王喜。
units.en: In the winter of the seventh year, the Emperor personally led a campaign against him, defeating Xin's army at Tongdi and beheading his general Wang Xi.
units.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, the Emperor personally went to attack, defeated Xin's army at Tongdi, and beheaded his general Wang Xi.

units.zh: 信亡走匈奴。
units.en: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.

units.zh: （與）其與白土人曼丘臣、王黃等立趙苗裔趙利為王，復收信敗散兵，而與信及冒頓謀攻漢。
units.en: Together with Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang, men of Baitu, they set up Zhao Li, a scion of the Zhao royal house, as king. They rallied Xin's defeated and scattered troops and, together with Xin and Modu, plotted to attack Han.
units.literal: He and Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang, men of Baitu, established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao royal line, as king, gathered Xin's defeated and scattered troops, and together with Xin and Modu plotted to attack Han.

units.zh: 匈奴仗左右賢王將萬餘騎與王黃等屯廣武以南，至晉陽，與漢兵戰，漢大破之，追至于離石，復破之。
units.en: The Xiongnu deployed their Wise Kings of the Left and Right with more than ten thousand cavalry, who joined Wang Huang's forces and encamped south of Guangwu, advancing as far as Jinyang. They engaged the Han army, but Han won a decisive victory, pursuing them to Lishi and defeating them once more.
units.literal: The Xiongnu deployed the Wise Kings of the Left and Right leading more than ten thousand cavalry with Wang Huang and others to encamp south of Guangwu, reaching Jinyang, where they fought the Han army. Han inflicted a great defeat on them, pursued them to Lishi, and defeated them again.

units.zh: 匈奴復聚兵樓煩西北，漢令車騎擊破匈奴。
units.en: The Xiongnu reassembled their forces to the northwest of Loufan, but Han sent its chariots and cavalry to attack and rout them.
units.literal: The Xiongnu reassembled their troops northwest of Loufan; Han ordered chariots and cavalry to attack and defeat the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 匈奴常敗走，漢乘勝追北，聞冒頓居代（上）谷，高皇帝居晉陽，使人視冒頓，還報曰「可擊」。
units.en: The Xiongnu suffered defeat after defeat and retreated. Han pressed its advantage and pursued northward. Hearing that Modu was encamped in the Dai Valley, the High Emperor, based at Jinyang, sent scouts to assess his forces. They returned and reported: 'He can be attacked.'
units.literal: The Xiongnu were constantly defeated and fled; Han pursued in victory. Hearing that Modu was stationed in the Dai Valley, the High Emperor, staying at Jinyang, sent scouts to observe Modu; they returned and reported: 'He can be attacked.'

units.zh: 上遂至平城。
units.en: The Emperor then advanced to Pingcheng.
units.literal: The Emperor then advanced to Pingcheng.

units.zh: 上出白登，匈奴騎圍上，上乃使人厚遺閼氏。
units.en: The Emperor rode out to Baideng, where the Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him. He then sent an envoy to present lavish gifts to the Chanyu's consort.
units.literal: The Emperor went out to Baideng, and the Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him. The Emperor then sent someone to present lavish gifts to the Chanyu's consort.

units.zh: 閼氏乃說冒頓曰：「今得漢地，猶不能居；
units.en: The consort persuaded Modu, saying: 'Even if you were to seize the Han lands, you could not hold them.
units.literal: The consort then persuaded Modu, saying: 'Even if you take the Han lands, you still could not dwell there;

units.zh: 且兩主不相緱」居七日，胡騎稍引去。
units.en: Moreover, two rulers should not press each other into a corner.' After seven days, the Xiongnu cavalry gradually withdrew.
units.literal: Moreover, two rulers should not corner each other.' After seven days, the Hu cavalry gradually withdrew.

units.zh: 時天大霧，漢使人往來，胡不覺。
units.en: A thick fog had descended, and the Han envoys were able to pass back and forth without the Xiongnu noticing.
units.literal: At the time there was a great fog; Han sent people to come and go, and the Hu did not notice.

units.zh: 護軍中尉陳平言上曰：「胡者全兵，請令彊弩傅兩矢外向，徐行出圍。」
units.en: Chen Ping, the Commandant of the Guard, advised the Emperor: 'The Xiongnu still have their forces intact around us. I suggest we order our strongest crossbowmen to load two bolts apiece, facing outward, and march slowly out of the encirclement.'
units.literal: The Commandant of the Guard, Chen Ping, said to the Emperor: 'The Hu keep their troops intact; I request that we order the strong crossbowmen to load two bolts facing outward and slowly march out of the encirclement.'

units.zh: 入平城，漢救兵亦到，胡騎遂解去。
units.en: They reached Pingcheng, where the Han relief forces had also arrived, and the Xiongnu cavalry broke off and withdrew.
units.literal: They entered Pingcheng; the Han relief forces also arrived, and the Hu cavalry thereupon dispersed and withdrew.

units.zh: 漢亦罷兵歸。
units.en: The Han forces withdrew as well.
units.literal: Han also withdrew its troops and returned.

units.zh: 韓信為匈奴將兵往來擊邊。
units.en: Han Xin now served as a general for the Xiongnu, leading raids back and forth along the border.
units.literal: Han Xin served as a Xiongnu general, leading troops back and forth to attack the border.

units.zh: 漢十年，信令王黃等說誤陳豨。
units.en: In the tenth year of the Han dynasty, Xin had Wang Huang and others persuade and lead Chen Xi astray.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Han, Xin had Wang Huang and others persuade and mislead Chen Xi.

units.zh: 十一年春，故韓王信復與胡騎入居參合，距漢。
units.en: In the spring of the eleventh year, the former King of Han, Xin, once again rode in with Xiongnu cavalry and occupied Canhe, defying Han.
units.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, the former King of Han, Xin, again entered with Hu cavalry and occupied Canhe, resisting Han.

units.zh: 漢使柴將軍擊之，遺信書曰：「陛下寬仁，諸侯雖有畔亡，而復歸，輒復故位號，不誅也。
units.en: Han sent General Chai to attack him. Chai sent a letter to Xin, saying: 'His Majesty is generous and benevolent. When lords have rebelled and fled but later returned, he has always restored their former titles and ranks without executing them.
units.literal: Han sent General Chai to attack him. He sent Xin a letter saying: 'His Majesty is generous and benevolent; when lords have rebelled and fled but returned, he has always restored their former titles and ranks, without executing them.

units.zh: 大王所知。
units.en: As you well know, Great King.
units.literal: This the Great King knows.

units.zh: 今王以敗亡走胡，非有大罪，急自歸！」
units.en: Now you fled to the Xiongnu after a defeat—this is not a grave crime. Return at once!'
units.literal: Now the King, having been defeated and fled to the Hu, has not committed a great crime; hurry and return of your own accord!'

units.zh: 韓王信報曰：「陛下擢仆起閭巷，南面稱孤，此仆之幸也。
units.en: Han Xin the King of Han replied: 'His Majesty raised me from the common lanes to sit upon a throne facing south and bear the title of king. That was my great fortune.
units.literal: Han King Xin replied: 'His Majesty raised me from the common lanes, to face south and be addressed as the Solitary One; this was my good fortune.

units.zh: 滎陽之事，仆不能死，囚於項籍，此一罪也。
units.en: At the siege of Xingyang, I could not manage to die but was taken prisoner by Xiang Ji. That is my first crime.
units.literal: In the affair at Xingyang, I was unable to die but was captured by Xiang Ji; this is my first crime.

units.zh: 及寇攻馬邑，仆不能堅守，以城降之，此二罪也。
units.en: When the enemy attacked Mayi, I could not hold the city and surrendered it to them. That is my second crime.
units.literal: When the enemy attacked Mayi, I was unable to defend it firmly and surrendered the city to them; this is my second crime.

units.zh: 今反為寇將兵，與將軍爭一旦之命，此三罪也。
units.en: Now I have turned to lead enemy troops and contend with you, General, for our lives in a single morning's battle. That is my third crime.
units.literal: Now I have turned to lead enemy troops, contending with the General for survival on a single morning; this is my third crime.

units.zh: 夫種、蠡無一罪，身死亡；
units.en: Wen Zhong and Fan Li bore not a single crime, yet one was put to death and the other forced to flee.
units.literal: Wen Zhong and Fan Li had not a single crime, yet they died or fled.

units.zh: 今仆有三罪於陛下，而欲求活於世，此伍子胥所以僨於吳也。
units.en: Now I bear three crimes against His Majesty and yet wish to go on living. This is precisely what brought Wu Zixu to his destruction in Wu.
units.literal: Now I bear three crimes against His Majesty, yet wish to seek to live in the world; this is the reason Wu Zixu met his ruin in Wu.

units.zh: 今仆亡匿山谷閒，旦暮乞貸蠻夷，仆之思歸，如痿人不忘起，盲者不忘視也，勢不可耳。」
units.en: Now I hide among the mountain valleys, begging sustenance from the barbarians morning and evening. My longing to return home is like the cripple who never stops dreaming of walking, or the blind man who never stops dreaming of sight—but my circumstances will not permit it.'
units.literal: Now I hide in the mountain valleys, begging from the barbarians morning and evening. My longing to return is like the lame who never forget walking, or the blind who never forget sight—but circumstances will not allow it.'

units.zh: 遂戰。
units.en: And so they fought.
units.literal: They then fought.

units.zh: 柴將軍屠參合，斬韓王信。
units.en: General Chai stormed Canhe and beheaded Han Xin, the King of Han.
units.literal: General Chai sacked Canhe and beheaded Han King Xin.

units.zh: 信之入匈奴，與太子俱；
units.en: When Xin went over to the Xiongnu, he brought his crown prince with him.
units.literal: When Xin entered the Xiongnu lands, he brought the Crown Prince with him;

units.zh: 及至穨當城，生子，因名曰穨當。
units.en: When they reached the city of Tuidang, a son was born, and the boy was named Tuidang after the place.
units.literal: When they reached the city of Tuidang, a son was born, and so he was named Tuidang.

units.zh: 韓太子亦生子，命曰嬰。
units.en: The Han crown prince also had a son, whom he named Ying.
units.literal: The Han Crown Prince also had a son, whom he named Ying.

units.zh: 至孝文十四年，穨當及嬰率其眾降漢。
units.en: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Tuidang and Ying led their followers in submitting to Han.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen, Tuidang and Ying led their followers to surrender to Han.

units.zh: 漢封穨當為弓高侯，嬰為襄城侯。
units.en: Han enfeoffed Tuidang as the Marquis of Gonggao and Ying as the Marquis of Xiangcheng.
units.literal: Han enfeoffed Tuidang as Marquis of Gonggao and Ying as Marquis of Xiangcheng.

units.zh: 吳楚軍時，弓高侯功冠諸將。
units.en: During the Rebellion of Wu and Chu, the Marquis of Gonggao's achievements surpassed those of all the other generals.
units.literal: During the war against Wu and Chu, the Marquis of Gonggao's merits were foremost among all the generals.

units.zh: 傳子至孫，孫無子，失侯。
units.en: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson, but the grandson had no heir, and the marquisate was lost.
units.literal: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson; the grandson had no son, and the marquisate was lost.

units.zh: 嬰孫以不敬失侯。
units.en: Ying's grandson lost his marquisate on grounds of disrespect.
units.literal: Ying's grandson lost the marquisate for disrespect.

units.zh: 穨當孽孫韓嫣，貴幸，名富顯於當世。
units.en: Tuidang's descendant through a concubine's line, Han Yan, became a court favorite, and his name and wealth were renowned in his generation.
units.literal: Tuidang's descendant through a concubine's line, Han Yan, was honored and favored, and his name, wealth, and prominence were known in his time.

units.zh: 其弟說，再封，數稱將軍，卒為案道侯。
units.en: His younger brother Yue was enfeoffed a second time, served several times as general, and ultimately became the Marquis of Andao.
units.literal: His younger brother Yue was twice enfeoffed, served as general several times, and ultimately became the Marquis of Andao.

units.zh: 子代，歲餘坐法死。
units.en: His son succeeded him, but within a year was convicted of a crime and put to death.
units.literal: His son succeeded him; after more than a year, he was convicted of a crime and executed.

units.zh: 後歲餘，說孫曾拜為龍頟侯，續說後。
units.en: More than a year later, Yue's grandson Zeng was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Longe to continue Yue's line.
units.literal: More than a year later, Yue's grandson Zeng was appointed Marquis of Longe, continuing Yue's line.

units.zh: 盧綰者，豐人也，與高祖同里。
units.en: Lu Wan was a native of Feng and came from the same village as the High Ancestor.
units.literal: Lu Wan was a man of Feng, from the same village as the High Ancestor.

units.zh: 盧綰親與高祖太上皇相愛，及生男，高祖、盧綰同日生，里中持羊酒賀兩家。
units.en: Lu Wan's parents were close friends with the High Ancestor's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor. When both families had sons, the High Ancestor and Lu Wan were born on the same day, and the villagers brought lamb and wine to congratulate both households.
units.literal: Lu Wan's parents and the High Ancestor's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, were close friends. When their sons were born, the High Ancestor and Lu Wan were born on the same day, and the villagers brought lamb and wine to congratulate both families.

units.zh: 及高祖、盧綰壯，俱學書，又相愛也。
units.en: When the High Ancestor and Lu Wan came of age, they studied together and grew fond of each other.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor and Lu Wan grew up, they studied together, and they were fond of each other.

units.zh: 里中嘉兩家親相愛，生子同日，壯又相愛，復賀兩家羊酒。
units.en: The villagers marveled that the two families had been close friends, that their sons were born on the same day, and that the boys grew up devoted to each other. Once again they brought lamb and wine to congratulate both households.
units.literal: The villagers, delighted that the two families were close and their sons born on the same day grew up fond of each other, again congratulated both families with lamb and wine.

units.zh: 高祖為布衣時，有吏事辟匿，盧綰常隨出入上下。
units.en: When the High Ancestor was still a commoner and had to go into hiding over legal troubles, Lu Wan always accompanied him wherever he went.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor was a commoner and had to flee and hide because of legal troubles, Lu Wan always accompanied him wherever he went.

units.zh: 及高祖初起沛，盧綰以客從，入漢中為將軍，常侍中。
units.en: When the High Ancestor first rose in revolt at Pei, Lu Wan followed as a retainer. He entered Hanzhong, was made a general, and attended constantly at court.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor first rose in revolt at Pei, Lu Wan followed as a retainer, entered Hanzhong and was made a general, and constantly attended at court.

units.zh: 從東擊項籍，以太尉常從，出入臥內，衣被飲食賞賜，群臣莫敢望，雖蕭曹等，特以事見禮，至其親幸，莫及盧綰。
units.en: He followed the eastward campaign against Xiang Ji, serving as Grand Commandant and constantly at the Emperor's side, even entering the private chambers. In clothing, bedding, food, drink, and gifts bestowed, no minister dared aspire to his level. Even Xiao He and Cao Shen were only accorded respect on account of their official duties—when it came to intimate favor, none could match Lu Wan.
units.literal: He followed the eastward campaign against Xiang Ji, and as Grand Commandant he constantly attended, going in and out of the bedchamber. In clothing, bedding, food, drink, and gifts, no minister dared aspire to his level. Even Xiao He and Cao Shen were only treated with ceremony on account of their duties; as for intimate favor, none could match Lu Wan.

units.zh: 綰封為長安侯。
units.en: Lu Wan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an.
units.literal: Wan was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Chang'an.

units.zh: 長安，故咸陽也。
units.en: Chang'an was the site of the former Xianyang.
units.literal: Chang'an was the former Xianyang.

units.zh: 漢五年冬，以破項籍，乃使盧綰別將，與劉賈擊臨江王共尉，破之。
units.en: In the winter of the fifth year of the Han dynasty, after the defeat of Xiang Ji, the Emperor dispatched Lu Wan to command a separate force. Together with Liu Jia, he attacked and defeated Gong Wei, the King of Linjiang.
units.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Han, after defeating Xiang Ji, he sent Lu Wan to command a separate force, joining Liu Jia to attack Gong Wei, the King of Linjiang, and defeated him.

units.zh: 七月還，從擊燕王臧荼，臧荼降。
units.en: In the seventh month he returned and joined the campaign against Zang Tu, the King of Yan. Zang Tu surrendered.
units.literal: In the seventh month he returned, and joined in attacking Zang Tu, the King of Yan; Zang Tu surrendered.

units.zh: 高祖已定天下，諸侯非劉氏而王者七人。
units.en: After the High Ancestor had settled the realm, there were seven men who held the title of king yet were not of the Liu surname.
units.literal: After the High Ancestor had settled the realm, there were seven lords who were kings but not of the Liu surname.

units.zh: 欲王盧綰，為群臣觖望。
units.en: He wished to make Lu Wan a king, but this aroused resentment among his ministers.
units.literal: He wished to make Lu Wan a king, but this caused resentment among his ministers.

units.zh: 及虜臧荼，乃下詔諸將相列侯，擇群臣有功者以為燕王。
units.en: After Zang Tu's capture, the Emperor issued a decree to his generals, ministers, and marquises, directing them to select a meritorious minister to serve as King of Yan.
units.literal: After capturing Zang Tu, he issued a decree to the generals, ministers, and marquises, to select a meritorious minister to be King of Yan.

units.zh: 群臣知上欲王盧綰，皆言曰：「太尉長安侯盧綰常從平定天下，功最多，可王燕。」
units.en: The ministers, knowing the Emperor wished to make Lu Wan king, all declared: 'The Grand Commandant, the Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Wan, has followed the Emperor throughout the pacification of the realm and has the greatest merit. He should be made King of Yan.'
units.literal: The ministers, knowing the Emperor wished to make Lu Wan king, all said: 'The Grand Commandant, the Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Wan, has constantly followed in pacifying the realm and has the most merit; he may be made King of Yan.'

units.zh: 詔許之。
units.en: The Emperor issued an edict granting the request.
units.literal: An edict approved it.

units.zh: 漢五年八月，乃立虜綰為燕王。
units.en: In the eighth month of the fifth year of the Han dynasty, Lu Wan was established as King of Yan.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Han, Lu Wan was established as King of Yan.

units.zh: 諸侯王得幸莫如燕王。
units.en: Of all the vassal kings, none enjoyed greater imperial favor than the King of Yan.
units.literal: Among the lords who were kings, none was as favored as the King of Yan.

units.zh: 漢十一年秋，陳豨反代地，高祖如邯鄲擊豨兵，燕王綰亦擊其東北。
units.en: In the autumn of the eleventh year, Chen Xi rebelled in the territory of Dai. The High Ancestor marched to Handan to attack Chen Xi's forces, and the King of Yan, Wan, also struck at his northeastern flank.
units.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year of Han, Chen Xi rebelled in the territory of Dai. The High Ancestor went to Handan to attack Xi's forces, and the King of Yan, Wan, also attacked his northeast.

units.zh: 當是時，陳豨使王黃求救匈奴。
units.en: At this time, Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to request assistance from the Xiongnu.
units.literal: At that time, Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to seek aid from the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 燕王綰亦使其臣張勝於匈奴，言豨等軍破。
units.en: The King of Yan also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu to report that Chen Xi's army had been defeated.
units.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu to announce that Xi's army had been defeated.

units.zh: 張勝至胡，故燕王臧茶子衍出亡在胡，見張勝曰：「公所以重於燕者，以習胡事也。
units.en: When Zhang Sheng reached the Xiongnu lands, Yan, the son of the former King of Yan Zang Tu, who had fled and was living among the Xiongnu, met him and said: 'The reason you are valued in Yan is that you understand the affairs of the northern peoples.
units.literal: When Zhang Sheng reached the Hu lands, Yan, the son of the former King of Yan Zang Tu, who had fled and was living among the Hu, met Zhang Sheng and said: 'The reason you are valued by Yan is that you understand the affairs of the Hu.

units.zh: 燕所以久存者，以諸侯數反，兵連不決也。
units.en: The reason Yan has survived so long is that the various lords have frequently rebelled, keeping the armies tied down without a decisive resolution.
units.literal: The reason Yan has long survived is that the lords have frequently rebelled, keeping the armies engaged without resolution.

units.zh: 今公為燕欲急滅豨等，豨等已盡，次亦至燕，公等亦且為虜矣。
units.en: Now you act on Yan's behalf, eager to destroy Chen Xi and his allies. But once they are finished, the court will turn its attention to Yan, and you and the others will become prisoners.
units.literal: Now you act on Yan's behalf and wish to quickly destroy Xi and the rest; once Xi and the rest are finished, the next target will be Yan, and you and the others will become prisoners.

units.zh: 公何不令燕且緩陳豨而與胡和？
units.en: Why not have Yan ease up on the campaign against Chen Xi and make peace with the Xiongnu?
units.literal: Why don't you have Yan slow its campaign against Chen Xi and make peace with the Hu?

units.zh: 事寬，得長王燕；
units.en: If the situation relaxes, you can remain king of Yan for a long time.
units.literal: If things ease, you can long remain king of Yan;

units.zh: 即有漢急，可以安國。」
units.en: And should Han press you, you will have the means to keep the state secure.'
units.literal: If there is urgency from Han, you can keep the state secure.'

units.zh: 張勝以為然，豨私令匈奴助豨等擊燕。
units.en: Zhang Sheng found this reasoning persuasive. Chen Xi secretly ordered the Xiongnu to assist his forces in raiding Yan.
units.literal: Zhang Sheng thought this was right; Chen Xi secretly ordered the Xiongnu to help Xi and the others attack Yan.

units.zh: 燕王綰疑張勝與胡反，上書請族張勝。
units.en: The King of Yan suspected Zhang Sheng of conspiring with the Xiongnu to rebel and submitted a memorial requesting that Zhang Sheng's entire clan be executed.
units.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, suspected Zhang Sheng of conspiring with the Hu to rebel, and submitted a memorial requesting the execution of Zhang Sheng's entire clan.

units.zh: 勝還，具道所以為者。
units.en: When Zhang Sheng returned, he explained the full reasoning behind his actions.
units.literal: Sheng returned and fully explained the reasons for his actions.

units.zh: 燕王寤，乃詐論它人，脫勝家屬，使得為匈奴閒，而陰使范齊之陳豨所，欲令久亡，連兵勿決。
units.en: The King of Yan came to understand and so framed another man in Zhang Sheng's place, freed Sheng's family, and had Sheng serve as a liaison with the Xiongnu. Meanwhile, he secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp, intending to prolong the conflict and keep the armies locked in an unresolved stalemate.
units.literal: The King of Yan understood, and so fraudulently convicted another person, freed Sheng's family, and had Sheng serve as an agent between the Xiongnu, while secretly sending Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp, wishing to prolong the conflict and keep the armies engaged without resolution.

units.zh: 漢十二年，東擊黥布，豨常將兵居代，漢使樊噲擊斬豨。
units.en: In the twelfth year, while the Emperor campaigned east against Qing Bu, Chen Xi continued to hold Dai with his forces. Han sent Fan Kuai to attack and behead Chen Xi.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Han, during the eastern campaign against Qing Bu, Xi continued to command troops in Dai. Han sent Fan Kuai to attack and behead Xi.

units.zh: 其裨將降，言燕王綰使范齊通計謀於豨所。
units.en: One of Chen Xi's subordinate generals surrendered and revealed that the King of Yan had sent Fan Qi to coordinate plots with Chen Xi.
units.literal: One of Xi's subordinate generals surrendered and reported that the King of Yan, Wan, had sent Fan Qi to communicate plots with Xi.

units.zh: 高祖使使召盧綰，綰稱病。
units.en: The High Ancestor sent a messenger to summon Lu Wan, but Wan pleaded illness.
units.literal: The High Ancestor sent an envoy to summon Lu Wan; Wan pleaded illness.

units.zh: 上又使辟陽侯審食其、御史大夫趙堯往迎燕王，因驗問左右。
units.en: The Emperor then sent the Marquis of Biyang, Shen Shiqi, and the Grand Censor Zhao Yao to receive the King of Yan and to investigate and interrogate his attendants.
units.literal: The Emperor also sent the Marquis of Biyang, Shen Shiqi, and the Grand Censor Zhao Yao to go and receive the King of Yan, and to investigate and question those around him.

units.zh: 綰愈恐，閉匿，謂其幸臣曰：「非劉氏而王，獨我與長沙耳。
units.en: Wan grew even more fearful and shut himself away. He confided to his trusted ministers: 'Of those who bear the title of king without being of the Liu surname, only I and the King of Changsha remain.
units.literal: Wan grew more afraid and shut himself away in hiding. He said to his favored ministers: 'Among those who are kings but not of the Liu surname, only I and the King of Changsha remain.

units.zh: 往年春，漢族淮陰，夏，誅彭越，皆呂后計。
units.en: Last spring, the court destroyed the clan of the Marquis of Huaiyin. That summer, Peng Yue was executed. Both were the schemes of Empress Lu.
units.literal: Last year in spring, Han exterminated the clan of the Marquis of Huaiyin; in summer, Peng Yue was executed—all were Empress Lu's schemes.

units.zh: 今上病，屬任呂后。
units.en: Now the Emperor is ill and has entrusted affairs of state to Empress Lu.
units.literal: Now the Emperor is ill and has entrusted affairs to Empress Lu.

units.zh: 呂后婦人，專欲以事誅異姓王者及大功臣。」
units.en: Empress Lu is a woman bent on finding pretexts to execute kings of other surnames and great meritorious ministers.'
units.literal: Empress Lu is a woman who desires only to find pretexts to execute kings of different surnames and great meritorious ministers.'

units.zh: 乃遂稱病不行。
units.en: And so he continued to plead illness and refused to go.
units.literal: He thereupon continued to plead illness and did not go.

units.zh: 其左右皆亡匿。
units.en: His attendants all fled and went into hiding.
units.literal: All those around him fled and went into hiding.

units.zh: 語頗泄，辟陽侯聞之，歸具報上，上益怒。
units.en: Word of this leaked out. The Marquis of Biyang heard the report, returned to court, and relayed everything to the Emperor. The Emperor's anger only deepened.
units.literal: Word of this leaked; the Marquis of Biyang heard of it, returned and reported everything to the Emperor, and the Emperor grew more angry.

units.zh: 又得匈奴降者，降者言張勝亡在匈奴，為燕使。
units.en: Furthermore, a Xiongnu defector was captured, and the defector reported that Zhang Sheng had fled to the Xiongnu, where he was serving as an envoy of Yan.
units.literal: Moreover, a Xiongnu defector was captured, and the defector said Zhang Sheng had fled and was among the Xiongnu, serving as an envoy of Yan.

units.zh: 於是上曰：「盧綰果反矣！」
units.en: At this, the Emperor declared: 'Lu Wan has indeed rebelled!'
units.literal: Thereupon the Emperor said: 'Lu Wan has indeed rebelled!'

units.zh: 使樊噲擊燕。
units.en: He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.
units.literal: He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.

units.zh: 燕王綰悉將其宮人家屬騎數千居長城下，侯伺，幸上病愈，自入謝。
units.en: The King of Yan gathered all his palace women and family members, along with several thousand horsemen, and camped below the Great Wall, watching and waiting, hoping that the Emperor would recover so he could go in person to beg forgiveness.
units.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, took all his palace women and family members with several thousand cavalry to camp below the Great Wall, waiting and watching, hoping the Emperor would recover from his illness so he could personally go and offer his apologies.

units.zh: 四月，高祖崩，盧綰遂將其眾亡入匈奴，匈奴以為東胡盧王。
units.en: In the fourth month, the High Ancestor died. Lu Wan then led his followers across the border into Xiongnu territory. The Xiongnu made him King Lu of the Eastern Hu.
units.literal: In the fourth month, the High Ancestor died. Lu Wan thereupon led his followers to flee into the Xiongnu lands. The Xiongnu made him King Lu of the Eastern Hu.

units.zh: 綰為蠻夷所侵奪，常思復歸。
units.en: Among the barbarians, Wan was constantly harassed and plundered, and he never stopped longing to return home.
units.literal: Wan was encroached upon and plundered by the barbarians, and he constantly thought of returning.

units.zh: 居歲餘，死胡中。
units.en: After little more than a year, he died among the Xiongnu.
units.literal: After more than a year, he died among the Hu.

units.zh: 高后時，盧綰妻子亡降漢，會高后病，不能見，舍燕邸，為欲置酒見之。
units.en: During Empress Gao's regency, Lu Wan's wife and children fled and surrendered to Han. But as it happened, Empress Gao was ill and could not receive them. She lodged them at the Yan residence, intending to hold a banquet to meet them.
units.literal: During the time of Empress Gao, Lu Wan's wife and children fled and surrendered to Han. It happened that Empress Gao was ill and could not receive them, so she lodged them at the Yan residence, intending to arrange a banquet to meet them.

units.zh: 高祖竟崩，不得見。
units.en: The High Ancestor was already dead, and so they never met him.
units.literal: The High Ancestor had already died, and they could not meet him.

units.zh: 盧綰妻亦病死。
units.en: Lu Wan's wife also became ill and died.
units.literal: Lu Wan's wife also fell ill and died.

units.zh: 孝景中六年，盧綰孫他之，以東胡王降，封為亞谷侯。
units.en: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing, Lu Wan's grandson Tazhi surrendered in his capacity as King of the Eastern Hu and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yagu.
units.literal: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Lu Wan's grandson Tazhi surrendered as King of the Eastern Hu and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yagu.

units.zh: 陳豨者，宛朐人也，不知始所以得從。
units.en: Chen Xi was a man of Wanqu. It is not known how he first came to enter service.
units.literal: Chen Xi was a man of Wanqu. It is not known how he first came to serve.

units.zh: 及高祖七年冬，韓王信反，入匈奴，上至平城還，乃封豨為列侯，以趙相國將監趙、代邊兵，邊兵皆屬焉。
units.en: In the winter of the High Ancestor's seventh year, after Han Xin the King of Han rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu and the Emperor had gone to Pingcheng and returned, Chen Xi was enfeoffed as a marquis and appointed Chancellor of Zhao with command over the border troops of Zhao and Dai. All the border forces were placed under his authority.
units.literal: In the winter of the High Ancestor's seventh year, when Han King Xin rebelled and went over to the Xiongnu and the Emperor went to Pingcheng and returned, Chen Xi was enfeoffed as a marquis, appointed as Chancellor of Zhao to command and supervise the border troops of Zhao and Dai; all the border troops were placed under his authority.

units.zh: 豨常告歸過趙，趙相周昌見豨賓客隨之者千餘乘，邯鄲官舍皆滿。
units.en: Chen Xi frequently took leave and passed through Zhao. The Chancellor of Zhao, Zhou Chang, observed that more than a thousand carriages of retainers accompanied him, and the official guesthouses of Handan were all full to overflowing.
units.literal: Xi often took leave and passed through Zhao. The Chancellor of Zhao, Zhou Chang, observed that more than a thousand carriages of retainers followed Xi, and the official guesthouses in Handan were all full.

units.zh: 豨所以待賓客布衣交，皆出客下。
units.en: Chen Xi treated his retainers with the humility of a man among equals, always placing himself below his guests in courtesy.
units.literal: Xi treated his retainers with the deference of a commoner's friendship, always placing himself beneath his guests.

units.zh: 豨還之代，周昌乃求入見。
units.en: When Chen Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang sought an audience with the Emperor.
units.literal: When Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang sought an audience with the Emperor.

units.zh: 見上，具言豨賓客盛甚，擅兵於外數歲，恐有變。
units.en: He had an audience with the Emperor and reported in full that Chen Xi's retinue was enormously large, that he had held military command far from the capital for several years, and that he feared trouble was brewing.
units.literal: He saw the Emperor and fully reported that Xi's retainers were exceedingly numerous, that he had held military authority outside for several years, and that he feared there would be trouble.

units.zh: 上乃令人覆案豨客居代者財物諸不法事，多連引豨。
units.en: The Emperor then ordered an investigation into the finances and illegal activities of Chen Xi's retainers residing in Dai. Many of the cases implicated Chen Xi.
units.literal: The Emperor then sent people to investigate and examine the finances and illegal activities of Xi's retainers residing in Dai; many of the cases implicated Xi.

units.zh: 豨恐，陰令客通使王黃、曼丘臣所。
units.en: Chen Xi grew fearful and secretly sent retainers to make contact with Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen.
units.literal: Xi grew afraid and secretly sent retainers to communicate with Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen.

units.zh: 及高祖十年七月，太上皇崩，使人召豨，豨稱病甚。
units.en: In the seventh month of the tenth year, the Grand Supreme Emperor died. A messenger was sent to summon Chen Xi, but he claimed he was gravely ill.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the High Ancestor's tenth year, the Grand Supreme Emperor died. A messenger was sent to summon Xi, but Xi claimed he was gravely ill.

units.zh: 九月，遂與王黃等反，自立為代王，劫略趙、代。
units.en: In the ninth month, he rebelled together with Wang Huang and the others, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and plundered the territories of Zhao and Dai.
units.literal: In the ninth month, he then rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai.

units.zh: 上聞，乃赦趙、代吏人為豨所詿誤劫略者，皆赦之。
units.en: When the Emperor heard the news, he pardoned all the officials and common people of Zhao and Dai who had been misled, deceived, or coerced by Chen Xi.
units.literal: When the Emperor heard, he pardoned the officials and people of Zhao and Dai who had been misled, deceived, or coerced by Xi; he pardoned them all.

units.zh: 上自往，至邯鄲，喜曰：「豨不南據漳水，北守邯鄲，知其無能為也。」
units.en: The Emperor went in person, and upon reaching Handan said with satisfaction: 'Chen Xi failed to hold the Zhang River to the south or defend Handan to the north. I know now that he is incapable of accomplishing anything.'
units.literal: The Emperor went in person, and upon reaching Handan said with pleasure: 'Xi did not hold the Zhang River in the south or defend Handan in the north; I know he is incapable of accomplishing anything.'

units.zh: 趙相奏斬常山守、尉，曰：「常山二十五城，豨反，亡其二十城。」
units.en: The Chancellor of Zhao memorialized requesting the execution of the Governor and Commandant of Changshan, saying: 'Changshan has twenty-five cities, and when Chen Xi rebelled, twenty of them were lost.'
units.literal: The Chancellor of Zhao memorialized requesting the execution of the Governor and Commandant of Changshan, saying: 'Changshan has twenty-five cities; when Xi rebelled, they lost twenty of them.'

units.zh: 上問曰：「守、尉反乎？」
units.en: The Emperor asked, 'Had the Governor and Commandant rebelled?'
units.literal: The Emperor asked: 'Did the Governor and Commandant rebel?'

units.zh: 對曰：「不反。」
units.en: The reply was: 'They did not rebel.'
units.literal: The reply was: 'They did not rebel.'

units.zh: 上曰：「是力不足也。」
units.en: The Emperor said: 'Then they simply lacked the strength to resist.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'Then their strength was insufficient.'

units.zh: 赦之，復以為常山守、尉。
units.en: The Emperor pardoned them and restored them as Governor and Commandant of Changshan.
units.literal: He pardoned them and reappointed them as Governor and Commandant of Changshan.

units.zh: 上問周昌曰：「趙亦有壯士可令將者乎？」
units.en: The Emperor asked Zhou Chang: 'Does Zhao have any brave men who could serve as generals?'
units.literal: The Emperor asked Zhou Chang: 'Does Zhao also have brave men who could serve as generals?'

units.zh: 對曰：「有四人。」
units.en: Zhou Chang replied: 'There are four men.'
units.literal: He replied: 'There are four men.'

units.zh: 四人謁，上謾罵曰：「豎子能為將乎？」
units.en: The four men came for an audience. The Emperor berated them, saying: 'Can rascals like you really serve as generals?'
units.literal: The four men came for an audience. The Emperor abused them, saying: 'Can scoundrels like you serve as generals?'

units.zh: 四人慚伏。
units.en: The four men hung their heads in shame.
units.literal: The four men bowed their heads in shame.

units.zh: 上封之各千戶，以為將。
units.en: The Emperor granted each of them a thousand-household fief and made them generals.
units.literal: The Emperor enfeoffed each of them with a thousand households and appointed them as generals.

units.zh: 左右諫曰：「從入蜀、漢，伐楚，功未遍行，今此何功而封？」
units.en: His advisors remonstrated: 'Many who followed you into Shu and Han and campaigned against Chu have not yet been rewarded. What merits have these men earned to deserve enfeoffment?'
units.literal: Those around him remonstrated, saying: 'Those who followed you into Shu and Han and campaigned against Chu have not all been rewarded; what merits do these men have to be enfeoffed?'

units.zh: 上曰：「非若所知！
units.en: The Emperor said, 'You do not understand this!
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'This is not something you understand!

units.zh: 陳豨反，邯鄲以北皆豨有，吾以羽檄徵天下兵，未有至者，今唯獨邯鄲中兵耳。
units.en: Chen Xi has rebelled, and everything north of Handan is in his hands. I sent urgent dispatches summoning troops from across the empire, but none have arrived. All I have now is the garrison of Handan.
units.literal: Chen Xi has rebelled, and everything north of Handan is under his control. I sent urgent dispatches summoning troops from the realm, but none have arrived. Now I have only the garrison of Handan.

units.zh: 吾胡愛四千戶封四人，不以慰趙子弟！」
units.en: How could I begrudge four thousand households to enfeoff four men, if it serves to hearten the men of Zhao!'
units.literal: How could I begrudge four thousand households to enfeoff four men, rather than use them to hearten the men of Zhao!'

units.zh: 皆曰：「善。」
units.en: Everyone agreed: 'Well said.'
units.literal: All said: 'Good.'

units.zh: 於是上曰：「陳豨將誰？」
units.en: The Emperor then asked: 'Who are Chen Xi's generals?'
units.literal: Thereupon the Emperor asked: 'Who are Chen Xi's generals?'

units.zh: 曰：「王黃、曼丘臣，皆故賈人。」
units.en: Those present replied: 'Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen. Both are former merchants.'
units.literal: The reply was: 'Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen; both are former merchants.'

units.zh: 上曰：「吾知之矣。」
units.en: The Emperor said, 'I understand the matter now.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'I know what to do.'

units.zh: 乃各以千金購黃、臣等。
units.en: He then placed a bounty of a thousand catties of gold each on the heads of Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and the others.
units.literal: He then offered a bounty of a thousand catties of gold each for Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and the others.

units.zh: 十一年冬，漢兵擊斬陳豨將侯敞、王黃於曲逆下，破豨將張春於聊城，斬首萬餘。
units.en: In the winter of the eleventh year, the Han army attacked and beheaded Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang below the walls of Quni, and defeated his general Zhang Chun at Liaocheng, taking more than ten thousand heads.
units.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, the Han army attacked and beheaded Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang below Quni, defeated Xi's general Zhang Chun at Liaocheng, and took more than ten thousand heads.

units.zh: 太尉勃入定太原、代地。
units.en: The Grand Commandant Bo marched in and pacified the territories of Taiyuan and Dai.
units.literal: The Grand Commandant Bo entered and pacified the territories of Taiyuan and Dai.

units.zh: 十二月，上自擊東垣，東垣不下，卒罵上；
units.en: In the twelfth month, the Emperor personally attacked Dongyuan. The city did not fall, and its soldiers hurled insults at the Emperor.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, the Emperor personally attacked Dongyuan. Dongyuan did not fall, and the soldiers cursed the Emperor.

units.zh: 東垣降，卒罵者斬之，不罵者黥之。
units.en: When Dongyuan surrendered, those soldiers who had hurled insults were beheaded, and those who had not hurled insults were branded.
units.literal: When Dongyuan surrendered, those soldiers who had cursed were beheaded, and those who had not cursed were branded.

units.zh: 更命東垣為真定。
units.en: He renamed Dongyuan as Zhending.
units.literal: He changed the name of Dongyuan to Zhending.

units.zh: 王黃、曼丘臣其麾下受購賞之，皆生得，以故陳豨軍遂敗。
units.en: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were captured alive by their own subordinates, who had been lured by the bounties. With their generals gone, Chen Xi's army collapsed.
units.literal: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were captured alive by those under their own command who had accepted the bounty reward; for this reason Chen Xi's army was ultimately defeated.

units.zh: 上還至洛陽。
units.en: The Emperor returned to Luoyang.
units.literal: The Emperor returned to Luoyang.

units.zh: 上曰：「代居常山北，趙乃從山南有之，遠。」
units.en: The Emperor said: 'Dai lies north of the Changshan Mountains, yet Zhao governs it from south of the range—too distant.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'Dai lies north of Changshan, yet Zhao governs it from south of the mountains; this is too far.'

units.zh: 乃立子恒為代王，都中都，代、鴈門皆屬代。
units.en: He thereupon established his son Heng as King of Dai, with the capital at Zhongdu. The territories of Dai and Yanmen were both placed under his authority.
units.literal: He then established his son Heng as King of Dai, with his capital at Zhongdu; Dai and Yanmen were both placed under Dai.

units.zh: 高祖十二年冬，樊噲軍卒追斬豨於靈丘。
units.en: In the winter of the twelfth year, soldiers under Fan Kuai's command pursued and beheaded Chen Xi at Lingqiu.
units.literal: In the winter of the High Ancestor's twelfth year, soldiers of Fan Kuai's army pursued and beheaded Xi at Lingqiu.

units.zh: 太史公曰：韓信、盧綰非素積德累善之世，徼一時權變，以詐力成功，遭漢初定，故得列地，南面稱孤。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Han Xin and Lu Wan came not from families that had long cultivated virtue and accumulated merit. They seized upon the expedient shifts of their time, winning success through cunning and force. It was only because they happened to live at the founding of the Han dynasty that they were able to receive territories, face south, and bear the title of king.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Han Xin and Lu Wan were not of families that had long accumulated virtue and good deeds. They seized upon the expedient changes of the moment, achieving success through cunning and force. Because they encountered the founding of the Han, they were able to receive territories, face south, and bear the title of king.

units.zh: 內見疑彊大，外倚蠻貊以為援，是以日疏自危，事窮智困，卒赴匈奴，豈不哀哉！
units.en: Within the empire they were suspected for their power; beyond the frontiers they relied on the barbarians for support. And so they grew more isolated with each passing day, placing themselves in ever greater peril, until their stratagems were exhausted, their wits confounded, and in the end they fled to the Xiongnu. Is this not cause for lament!
units.literal: Internally they were suspected for their strength and power; externally they relied on the barbarians for support. Thus, they grew daily more estranged and imperiled, until their stratagems were exhausted and their wits confounded, and they finally fled to the Xiongnu. Is this not lamentable!

units.zh: 陳豨，梁人，其少時數稱慕魏公子；
units.en: Chen Xi was a man of Liang who in his youth often professed his admiration for Lord Xinling of Wei.
units.literal: Chen Xi was a man of Liang. In his youth he often professed admiration for Lord Xinling of Wei.

units.zh: 及將軍守邊，招致賓客而下士，名聲過實。
units.en: When he served as a general guarding the frontier, he gathered retainers about him and humbled himself before men of worth, until his reputation far exceeded the reality.
units.literal: When he served as general guarding the border, he attracted retainers and humbled himself before men of worth, and his reputation exceeded his substance.

units.zh: 周昌疑之，疵瑕頗起，懼禍及身，邪人進說，遂陷無道。
units.en: Zhou Chang grew suspicious of him, and his failings increasingly came to light. Fearing that disaster would reach his own person, and swayed by the counsel of wicked men, he fell headlong into lawlessness.
units.literal: Zhou Chang grew suspicious of him; faults and flaws increasingly surfaced; fearing calamity would reach his person, and wicked men offering counsel, he fell into lawlessness.

units.zh: 於戲悲夫！
units.en: Alas, how tragic!
units.literal: Alas, how sad!

units.zh: 夫計之生孰成敗於人也深矣！
units.en: How profoundly do the schemes one conceives determine a person's success or ruin!
units.literal: How profoundly do the schemes one conceives determine success or failure in a person!
